access_notes.value: Requires a Zendesk account/subdomain; signup is self-serve via a free product trial, with no partner approval or sales contact evidenced. Individual APIs and features are plan-tier gated (e.g., Custom Objects API requires Support Enterprise or Suite Team plans and above; sandbox environments are listed only on the top support tier; a High Volume API add-on raises rate limits). Zendesk Bridge / external AI agent MCP connections are additionally in an early access program (EAP).
access_notes.quote: The Custom Objects API is available on Support Enterprise plans and Zendesk Suite Team plans and above.

official_mcp_server.quote: In your external agent's AI platform, connect your external AI agent to Zendesk with an MCP server URL specified in the connection you configured.

rate_limits.value: Plan-based: Support and Help Center API requests per minute: Team 200, Growth 400, Professional 400, Enterprise 700, Enterprise Plus 2500 (High Volume API add-on raises qualifying plans to 2500); plus per-endpoint limits (e.g., 30 updates per 10 minutes per user per ticket, incremental exports 10 req/min); excess returns 429 with Retry-After.
rate_limits.quote: Support and Help Center API requests per minute | 200 | 400 | 400 | 700 | 2500

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: APIs are path-versioned (v2, e.g. /api/v2/tickets.json) and Zendesk publishes API versioning documentation for its Conversations API; the general deprecation/sunset policy was not present in the captured evidence.

verdict_reason: Zendesk publishes a broad, well-documented public REST API with OAuth 2.0 (scope-based) and API token authentication, plus plan-documented rate limits and a 483-tool Composio toolkit. Credentials are self-serve: a free Zendesk trial/account with admin access is sufficient, with no partner approval or sales contact required. Some APIs and the sandbox environment are gated to higher plan tiers, but the core Support/Help Center API and OAuth setup are reachable without outreach.
open_questions: The webhooks documentation pages (developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/webhooks/introduction/) were in the search plan, but no page text was included in the evidence bundle, so webhooks support is left not_found.

A search snippet on support.zendesk.com indicates Zendesk is removing API tokens as an authentication method (unused tokens auto-deactivate July 28, 2026; all tokens stop working by April 30, 2027), but that page was not captured in SOURCES, so this sunset is not reflected in api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.

The vendor-operated Zendesk MCP Server is delivered via Zendesk Bridge and is currently in an early access program (EAP); the actual MCP server URL is provisioned per connection and is not published, so the docs URL is cited in official_mcp_server.
No community/third-party MCP servers were evidenced (MCP registry results empty; GitHub repository check returned no results), so community_mcp_servers is not_found rather than an empty list.
Pricing details (e.g., $19/agent/month starting price) and trial length appeared only in search snippets, not in the captured pricing page text, so they are excluded from claims.

Official SDK evidence covers Android, iOS, Unity, and a Web Widget SDK; server-side SDK languages (if any) were not evidenced, and the Web Widget clause was omitted from the quoted snippet for length.
Whether API access is fully available during the free trial (vs. only on paid plans) was not explicitly documented in the captured pages; access_model is therefore medium confidence.
